selection_reasoning: Mining a potted_red_tulip is a single atomic task that is clearly observable and verifiable. The agent needs to find and break a potted red tulip block in the scene. This task is straightforward to set up (place a potted red tulip in the scene), easy to verify (check if the block has been mined/removed), and doesn't require deep Minecraft domain knowledge — the agent just needs to locate the flower pot and break it. It's a clean, self-contained task suitable for a single-task benchmark.

milestones.description: Uses count_in_box_at_most (kind='block', max_count=0) to verify the potted_red_tulip block has been removed from its placement location. This rule type was chosen because: (1) when a potted plant is mined, it drops as separate items (flower_pot + red_tulip), NOT as 'potted_red_tulip', so inventory_has cannot directly check for the mined block; (2) block removal at the known position is the most direct and reliable verification that the mining action occurred. The box [-1,-1,-1] to [5,5,5] generously encompasses the tulip's known position at spawn-relative (2,2,2) with ±3 margin.

scene_description: A small stone brick platform with a decorative pedestal in one corner. The pedestal is made of oak planks topped with a potted red tulip, flanked by oak log pillars. The player spawns on the platform facing the general direction of the tulip and must walk over and mine it.
task_text: Find and mine the potted red tulip sitting on the wooden pedestal nearby.
design_notes: The potted_red_tulip is at relative position (~2, ~2, ~2) - two blocks above the player's foot level and 2 blocks to the side. It sits on an oak_planks block at (~2, ~1, ~2). Oak log pillars at the back and side create a decorative frame. The stone_bricks floor (~-3 to ~3, y=~0) provides a clear walking surface. The air fill ensures no obstructions between spawn and the target. The tulip is at eye-level height (y+2) making it easy to spot and mine. No tools required — flower pots break instantly with bare hands.
